state.heading: Which input gets which pack
state.text: wiring · steps 1–2 · the router and the label store Which input gets which pack A row matches when every key in its match shape equals the input. First match wins; no match returns null and the caller escalates. Only the declared state fields ever leave the machine. Each row has a fixture and the test in hub/wiring/test-routing.mjs asserts the route, the pack's existence in the catalog, and that nothing undeclared leaks into the state. Row Match Pack State fields sent Decided in code first Status Label store A row is one question on one item. It carries the jev_log columns with the address and subject replaced by a sender class and a hash, the model's typed answer, and who asserted the label: hand (the owner, through the review queue), implied (a named proxy rule over history), or none (a model answer waiting for a label). The three are counted separately and never pooled without saying so. Every live call through hub/wiring/ask.mjs --record leaves its none rows behind; the review queue and the extractor only add verdicts. Contract: label-schema.json ; writer: hub/wiring/label-store.mjs ; rows live in JEV-works/runs/labels/ . Column group Fields Rule
